argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical synthesis with reductio reconstruction and critical refutation

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The essay raises the objection that Tugushev may fall into indeterminism and responds by proposing an emergentist middle way; it also addresses the objection that literary examples support determinism by reinterpreting Kutuzov and Pierre.
objections_raised: If Tugushev rejects determinism, he falls into indeterminism or causa sui.
Emergent downward causation may be mysterious or incoherent.
Tolstoy's own literary examples (Kutuzov) appear to support determinism.

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: conceptual analysis, reductio reconstruction, literary case study, dialectical synthesis

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: free will, determinism, historical necessity, agency, emergence

structural_organization.structure_type: seven-part dialectical essay with introduction, exposition, critique, objection, constructive solution, application, conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay reconstructs Tolstoy's reductio against free will, exposes its hidden metaphysical presupposition (closed totality of being), uses Tugushev to critique that presupposition, confronts the danger of indeterminism, and resolves the dilemma by proposing an emergentist relational ontology of agency, illustrated through War and Peace.
